bull.b: Strong cloud growth, expanding remaining performance obligations, and NRR above 120% indicate durable subscription demand and customer expansion. These metrics support recurring revenue visibility, deeper product adoption, and continued growth across the next several quarters.

Atlassian converts its software revenue into substantial operating and free cash flow despite reported accounting losses. This cash generation supports product investment, AI development, and strategic flexibility while reducing reliance on external financing for ongoing growth.

Broad enterprise adoption of Rovo and rising assisted actions show that Atlassian is embedding AI into established workflows rather than relying solely on a standalone product. Greater platform usage can strengthen customer engagement, cross-selling, and strategic relevance.

bear.t: Persistent GAAP losses and weak operating profitability
bear.b: Atlassian’s strong gross margins and cash generation have not yet translated into consistent GAAP profitability. Persistent losses and volatile operating margins can constrain retained earnings, reduce returns to shareholders, and make durable earnings improvement dependent on cost discipline.

bear.t: Moderating FY27 growth and margin outlook
bear.b: Management’s FY27 outlook implies slower subscription ARR growth than the latest 23% result and materially lower profitability than Q4’s 12% GAAP operating margin. The planned moderation may limit near-term operating leverage while investment and execution priorities continue.

bear.t: Remaining leverage and negative shareholder returns
bear.b: Leverage has improved substantially but remains meaningful relative to equity, while negative ROE shows that accounting losses still weigh on shareholder returns. This reduces balance-sheet flexibility and leaves less capacity to absorb weaker results or fund initiatives internally.
